target_customer: Hospitality, food service, events and warehouse businesses that need hourly shift workers, and the hourly workers who take the shifts
problem: Businesses struggle to fill shifts quickly with reliable hourly workers, and workers lack easy ways to find local jobs.
business_model: Two-sided marketplace with a take rate on shifts booked through the app

founders.name: Sumir Meghani
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page; the company about page names no founders. Education and employers not found in sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile marketplace with matching, scheduling and payments; standard engineering with added trust and vetting operations.

defensibility.rationale: Local liquidity of workers and businesses builds a network effect, but multi-homing is easy and many staffing apps competed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it per sources found; it raised through 2023 and reports about 10 million workers in 2026.

market_need_then: Hospitality and hourly employers had frequent shift gaps; the company framed hiring as easy as ordering a ride or meal. No dated 2015 demand data was opened.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened

brand_strength.rationale: The name matches the Insta-style app naming of the era and is easy to say, but no source shows the brand itself driving growth.

outcome_analysis: Instawork grew from a hospitality shift app to a multi-industry staffing marketplace, raising $10M by 2018, $18M in 2019, $60M in 2021 and $60M at a reported $760M valuation in 2023. Press releases through 2026 describe double-digit shift growth and no layoffs or shutdown were found, so it is a growth-stage survivor with no exit yet.
notes: Series B label for the 2019 round comes from aggregator coverage; the GlobalVenturing article does not label it but describes earlier seed and Series A. WSJ via that article says Benchmark led an $8.2M Series A (included in the $10M). Sum of recorded rounds ($148M) is below the reported $160M total, so one earlier round may be missing. Series D label from the company post. Company about page says founded 2015 while the YC page says 2016. Founders: only one named; the 2019 article names none. Competitor search found only present-day comparison pages, nothing dated near 2015, so the list is empty.
